title: Bodycam Released After Officer Run Over
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

Before I became a cop, I used to think that police shootings always started with total mayhem, but they don't because sometimes they start with a conversation that suddenly stops working. There's a moment I would recognize immediately when cooperation ended and intent took its place, and it usually didn't start with anyone being loud or physical, and that's how this clip started. It's a subtle shift that cops learned to notice over time, so your attention sharpens and every angle suddenly matters, and your mind has to shift from handling the call to staying alive. Now, officers are generally trained not to shoot at vehicles, and the Department of Justice guidance says guns aren't for stopping cars by default. They only justify it when the vehicle itself is being used as deadly force and there's no realistic way to escape. Because once a driver points a car to a person, that's a weapon, because you can't grapple with a front bumper and you don't have time to negotiate with a windshield. And from a few feet away, there is no just step aside like some people might imagine. So the officer isn't thinking about charges anymore, he's thinking about not getting run over. Realistically, most police encounters end with paperwork. However, the ones where someone uses a vehicle as a weapon and with lives permanently changed, including the person who chose it.
